claims.text: Increasing aluminum content in DC magnetron-sputtered TiCrZrNbTa refractory high-entropy-alloy coatings improves high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Increasing aluminum content promotes formation of a protective Al2O3 surface scale.
The aluminum increase can improve oxidation resistance without compromising mechanical compatibility in service.
A low-aluminum TiCrZrNbTa refractory high-entropy-alloy coating is a standard or current coating for zirconium-alloy nuclear-fuel cladding.
The proposed structural mediator is a dense alumina scale.
The proposed alumina scale will adhere to the coating surface.
Added aluminum diffuses to the coating surface under high-temperature conditions.
Surface-enriched aluminum reacts with oxygen to form Al2O3.
The Al2O3 layer acts as a barrier that slows oxygen ingress.
Slower oxygen ingress reduces oxidation of the underlying coating or cladding material.
The increased-aluminum coating will produce at least a 30% reduction in oxidation mass gain relative to the low-aluminum baseline.
The increased-aluminum coating will produce at least a 30% reduction in oxide-scale thickness relative to the low-aluminum baseline.
The increased-aluminum coating will retain the mechanical properties required for fuel-cladding service.
The increased-aluminum coating will retain the thermal properties required for fuel-cladding service.
The proposed benefit is expected under oxidizing exposure at approximately 800°C to 1200°C.
Excessively high aluminum concentrations may cause detrimental phase formation.
Excessively high aluminum concentrations may degrade mechanical properties.
There is an aluminum-concentration range that enhances alumina formation without adversely affecting other coating properties.
